name: The Idoma from Apa, through Igala land

summary.text: Idoma tradition traces the clans to Apa, the Kwararafa country of the Jukun. Around 1500 they dispersed: the Agatu settled near the Benue, and others moved on to Idah. After a power struggle at Idah, about 1625, groups left north (the Alago) and south, and the western Idoma kingdoms, Igumale, Agila, Ugboju and Adoka among them, took shape around 1650.

routes.label: From Apa: the Agatu settle near the Benue
After a power struggle at Idah, the Alago ancestors go north to Doma

moments.title: Igumale
moments.text: Igumale is among the western Idoma kingdoms founded around 1650. It later took its ruler’s staff from the Attah.

moments.title: Agila
moments.text: Agila, in today’s Ado, is founded in the same wave.

moments.title: Ugboju
moments.text: Ugboju, led by Edor the great, became the nucleus for later groups such as Okpiko and Onyagede.

moments.title: Adoka
moments.text: Adoka is founded in the same wave.

note: Dates and routes follow one published timeline of Idoma history; Idoma clans tell their migrations in many versions.
